animation_preview.scope: Actual public source playback driven from monotonic callback gaps; sparse screenshots captured at observed times and encoded with timestamp quantization, final frame duplicated. This is not proof of source-reference visual cadence.
animation_preview.publication_policy: Diagnostic sparse capture only; do not present as a smooth or frame-rate-matched comparison.

limits: Numerical GPU checks sample three source vertices per primitive at four phases, and full index connectivity; they do not prove all vertices or exact raster winding.
Draco uses separate official JS/WASM decoder with shared codec ancestry; meshopt uses the same native codec as producer. Pose arithmetic is separately implemented.
Camera is a 192px orthographic inferred view with a framework point and directional light, not the upstream unknown camera/light/exposure. User visual approval remains pending.
Real-time preview covers only the glTF source form, 61 sparse captures over one observed loop; no performance target or dense reference-cadence claim.
Compiled fixture bytes were generated and loaded but not separately hashed in the public receipt.
The historic SIGSEGV did not recur in these cases; its root cause remains unknown.
Windows, editor parity, full material conformance and performance remain untested.

still_comparison.purpose: Review articulated robot source material and silhouette; upstream GIF is context, not a matched pixel or pose oracle.
still_comparison.limits: The GIF first frame animation phase is unknown, and camera, lighting and exposure are inferred; pose correspondence is not established.

deterministic_preview.purpose: Six-second actual public Model.Load and SkinnedModelRenderer source-material preview; each frame was independently rendered after a deterministic time seek. Not evidence of real-time playback or a matched upstream reference phase.
deterministic_preview.camera_limit: 192px orthographic inferred camera, framework point light and directional light; upstream camera and exposure unknown.
